title: Encrypting Email in Microsoft Outlook: When, How, and Best Practices
original_html:
When Should You Encrypt an Email? 

As you may be aware, York has Guidelines and Procedures for Use of Electronic Mail (E-mail) that state that by its nature, E-mail is not a confidential medium; it is possible for messages to be intercepted, modified, copied or redirected without the knowledge of the sender or recipient by those with sufficient access to the email transport systems or networks.  

Internal emails sent using Microsoft Outlook are already encrypted. Those using e-mail to transmit confidential and regulated data to external recipients (non-York email addresses) must use encryption technology approved by Information Security. Microsoft Outlook’s encryption feature is approved for use.  

Refer to the Information Security Classification Standard for what is considered mail confidential and regulated data.  

Encryption is required when sending sensitive, confidential or regulated data, for example:  

  • Financial data (bank details, invoices) 
  • Personally identifiable information 
  • Legal contracts or intellectual property 
  • Credit Card holder data 
  • Personal Health Information 
  • Identifiable research data 

Steps to Encrypt an Email External to York Recipients in Microsoft Outlook 

  1. Open Outlook and click New Email. 
  1. Go to the Options tab in the toolbar. 
  1. Click Encrypt (lock icon). 
  • If you see “Connect to Rights Management Servers and Get templates”, select it and wait for Outlook to update.
  • Choose Encrypt to protect content. A banner will appear at the top of your email stating that the message is encrypted and recipients can’t remove it. Visit Microsoft’s support page to read more about the encryption options.

Banner: 

  1. Compose and send your email as usual. 
  1. Your recipient will be able to open the email in any Outlook client. However, if the recipient is using a different email client, they may need to select a link and follow the steps provided to open the email. Learn more about this approach on Microsoft’s email encryption page. 

Best Practices for Encrypted Email Communication 

  • Notify the recipient in advance: Let them know to expect an encrypted email so they don’t mistake it for phishing. 
  • Verify recipient identity: Ensure you have the correct email address before sending. 
  • Limit sensitive content: Share only what is necessary. 
  • Follow University policies for compliance and retention: Policies, Procedures and Regulations - Secretariat Policies
